# @flatten-js/spatial-graph 2.0

> A 2D simple undirected Cartesian graph with private Graphology storage and
> mutable RBush candidate indexes. Nodes are coordinates; edges are straight
> segments. Queries return immutable SpatialNode/SpatialEdge snapshots.

## Read this first

This file describes the 2.0 API. Inspect the installed package version before
using these recipes in a 1.x project; 2.0 includes breaking changes.

Install @flatten-js/spatial-graph and its peer @flatten-js/core. ESM and CommonJS
are supported on Node.js 22+. Import from the package root only. For consumers,
this file, README.md, and dist/index.d.ts (ESM) / dist/index.d.cts (CJS) ship in the
package; examples/, docs/, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are repository-only material.
Use the declarations to resolve exact overloads and generic result types.
For contributors, AGENTS.md supplies repository commands and conventions;
CLAUDE.md imports that same file. Source examples need Node.js 22.18+.

## Elements, identity, and current state

<!-- example: snapshots.ts -->

```ts
import { SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';

// Coordinates identify nodes; queries return values captured at the time of query.
const graph = new SpatialGraph();
graph.addEdge(
  [
    [0, 0],
    [10, 0],
  ],
  { label: 'link' },
);
graph.addEdge([
  [10, 0],
  [10, 10],
]);

const node = graph.getNode([10, 0]);
const edge = graph.getEdgeBetween([0, 0], [10, 0]);
if (node && edge) {
  node.type; // 'corner'
  edge.midpoint; // [5, 0]
  edge.length; // 10
  graph.moveNode(node, [12, 0]);
  node.point; // retained snapshot: [10, 0]
  graph.getNode([10, 0]); // null
  graph.getNode([12, 0]); // fetch the current snapshot
}
```

- Point2D = readonly [x, y]; Segment2D = readonly [Point2D, Point2D]. A coordinate
  value does not imply membership. NodeInput/EdgeInput also accept snapshots.
  A snapshot input resolves its stored coordinates against CURRENT membership.
  Snapshots contain no graph pointer and have no mutation methods.
- Exact finite coordinates are the default. coordinatePrecision: 0 opts into
  the old integer grid; integers 0..15 quantize with Math.round and normalize -0.
  Scaled coordinate magnitudes must not exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER before
  rounding. Use graph.getNodeKey(point), never build or parse keys in user code.
- Coordinates define same-graph node equality. node.equals(other) compares keys;
  node.distanceTo(other) returns Euclidean distance. Edge equality compares
  undirected endpoints. Removing/recreating at one position compares equal.
  Cross-graph equality is outside the contract; ownership is not runtime-checked.
- Moving removes/recreates or merges positions. Retained snapshots do not follow
  the move; refetch by the destination. Metadata changes also require refetching.
- Snapshot coordinates and top-level attributes are copied/frozen. Nested values
  stay shared by default. cloneNodeAttributes/cloneEdgeAttributes isolate them.
- Classification: isolated=degree 0, stub=1, intermediate=straight degree 2,
  corner=bent degree 2, junction=3+. straightAngleToleranceDeg defaults to 1e-7
  degrees; positionTolerance defaults to 1e-9 graph units. Neither changes equality.
- Geometry crossings do not automatically create connectivity; call planarize()
  or splitEdge() to create the nodes. No faces or native curved edges are exposed.

## Metadata and result shapes

<!-- example: metadata.ts -->

```ts
import { SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';

interface NodeData {
  name: string;
}
interface EdgeData {
  width: number;
  weight?: number;
  label?: 'main' | 'secondary';
}

// Edges and splits create nodes implicitly, so required node fields need a factory.
const graph = new SpatialGraph<NodeData, EdgeData>({
  createNodeAttributes: () => ({ name: '' }),
});
const inserted = graph.addEdge(
  [
    [0, 0],
    [10, 0],
  ],
  { width: 3, weight: 999 },
);
if (inserted.status !== 'collapsed') {
  const width: number = inserted.edge.attributes.width;
  graph.mergeEdgeAttributes(inserted.edge, { width: width + 1 });
  graph.setEdgeLabel(inserted.edge, 'main');
}
```

Geometry and user attributes are separate. User x/type/length/weight fields do
not override node position, classification, or routing length. Required generic
node fields require createNodeAttributes for implicit endpoints and split nodes;
required attribute arguments cannot be omitted. Label setters retain string
unions; null removal requires an undefined-compatible label. Graph metadata uses
getGraphAttribute/setGraphAttribute/getGraphAttributes/replaceGraphAttributes.

| Operation | Result / absent case |
| --- | --- |
| getNode/getEdge/getEdgeBetween, element geometry/metadata getters | Snapshot/value or null |
| getNeighbors and subset collection queries | Array, empty when there are no matches |
| hasNode/hasEdge | boolean |
| removeNode/removeEdge/removeStubNode | boolean; false when absent or ineligible |
| removeNodes/removeEdges | Number removed; 0 when none |
| getGraphAttribute | Value or undefined |
| addNode | Snapshot; upserts supplied metadata |
| addEdge | {status: 'added' or 'existing', edge, endpoints}, or {status: 'collapsed', edge: null, endpoints} |
| addEdges | {results, added, existing, collapsed}; results follow input order |
| moveNode/moveNodes/mergeNodeInto | MutationReport, not the moved node |
| splitEdge/joinNode/collapseDegree2Node | Report with changed/reason and resulting elements |
| mergeNodeAttributes/mergeEdgeAttributes | Updated snapshot or null; never creates an element |
| getShortestPath/route | Structured result or null |

Invalid coordinates/options/callback results throw before mutation. Missing move
sources throw. Duplicate edge insertion preserves existing metadata; collapsed
edges create no endpoints. Node/edge counts and revision are read-only properties.

Moves are simultaneous, including swaps. Destination metadata wins, then the
smallest canonical source key; edge conflicts use original endpoint pairs.
Custom merge callbacks run during planning and cannot mutate the graph.
splitEdge validates exact AND canonical containment; missing/endpoint splits
are no-ops, off-edge splits throw. Metadata IDs are copied, never rewritten;
splitAttributes can supply application IDs. joinNode requires a straight degree-2
node without an existing neighbor edge; collapseDegree2Node explicitly permits
changing bends/triangles. Inspect the operation's report before using its elements.

## Traversal

`bfs(callback)` and `dfs(callback)` visit the whole graph, including isolated
nodes. `bfsFromNode(node, callback)` and `dfsFromNode(node, callback)` visit only
nodes reached from a tuple or snapshot; a missing start makes no visits. All
four return `void` and delegate to `graphology-traversal` on private adjacency.

Visitors receive `(SpatialNode, depth)`, with metadata on `node.attributes`.
BFS depth counts hops through the explored graph; DFS depth is discovery depth,
not minimum distance. Each traversal root starts at depth zero. Returning `true`
skips expansion of the current node; it does not cancel the traversal or visits
already queued. Whole-graph traversal may later start a new root among nodes
left unseen by pruning. Visitors must be synchronous and cannot mutate the graph
or start nested traversals. Ordinary reads such as `getNode()` are allowed.
Direction-mode options are omitted because SpatialGraph is undirected.

<!-- example: traversal.ts -->

```ts
import { SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';
import type { Point2D } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';

const graph = new SpatialGraph();
graph.addEdge([
  [0, 0],
  [1, 0],
]);
graph.addEdge([
  [0, 0],
  [0, 1],
]);
graph.addEdge([
  [1, 0],
  [2, 0],
]);
graph.addNode([99, 99]); // Isolated nodes are included by whole-graph traversals.

const breadth: Array<[Point2D, number]> = [];
graph.bfsFromNode([0, 0], (node, depth) => {
  breadth.push([node.point, depth]);
  return depth >= 1; // Skip expansion here; other queued nodes are still visited.
});
const depthFirst: Point2D[] = [];
graph.dfsFromNode(graph.getNode([0, 0])!, (node) => {
  depthFirst.push(node.point);
});
let breadthCount = 0;
let depthCount = 0;
graph.bfs(() => {
  breadthCount++;
});
graph.dfs(() => {
  depthCount++;
});
```

## Routing

getConnectedComponents() delegates directly to graphology-components on private
adjacency. It returns SpatialNode snapshot groups in Graphology DFS discovery
order, includes isolated nodes, and returns [] for an empty graph. This replaces
BFS node order; traversal-based labelling may change. A component is not a route.

<!-- example: routing.ts -->

```ts
import { PathAlgorithm, SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';

// Two alternatives: a short direct edge and a longer, cheaper detour.
const graph = new SpatialGraph();
graph.addEdges([
  {
    endpoints: [
      [0, 0],
      [20, 0],
    ],
    attributes: { fare: 10 },
  },
  {
    endpoints: [
      [0, 0],
      [0, 10],
    ],
    attributes: { fare: 1 },
  },
  {
    endpoints: [
      [0, 10],
      [20, 10],
    ],
    attributes: { fare: 1 },
  },
  {
    endpoints: [
      [20, 10],
      [20, 0],
    ],
    attributes: { fare: 1 },
  },
]);
const path = graph.getShortestPath([0, 0], [20, 0], { algorithm: PathAlgorithm.AStar });
const length = path?.length; // 20; missing/disconnected endpoints yield null.
```

PathAlgorithm.Dijkstra/derived length is the default; use PathAlgorithm.AStar
for A*. Import PathAlgorithm from the package root rather than spelling algorithm
strings. Both delegate to graphology-shortest-path; the spatial wrapper handles
validation and results. Cost callbacks return finite nonnegative
numbers or null to close an edge; zero is valid. Length and cost are independent.
A* supports reopening. Custom heuristics must be admissible, finite, nonnegative,
and zero at destination; admissibility is the caller's responsibility. Default A*
heuristic is Euclidean for length, zero for custom costs. Built-in routing accesses
the private graph directly and requires no toGraphology() call. Closed edges
are removed from a temporary copy, avoiding upstream null-weight coercion.

route(fromPoint, toPoint, {maxSnapDistance}) is nonmutating geometric routing
between exact nearest projections. It returns points, length, cost, from/to snap
results. Access distances are in from.distance/to.distance and are excluded from
length/cost. A temporary Graphology copy with projection nodes adds O(V+E)
time and space per query before search. This method does not accept custom
partial-edge costs.

## Snap and connect

<!-- example: snap-and-connect.ts -->

```ts
import { SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';

// Split first to make the projection a connected graph node, then add the spur.
const graph = new SpatialGraph();
graph.addEdge([
  [0, 0],
  [20, 0],
]);
const site = [4, 3] as const;
const nearest = graph.findNearestEdge(site);
if (nearest) {
  graph.splitEdge(nearest.edge, nearest.point);
  graph.addEdge([site, nearest.point]);
}
```

Nearest edge results include edge, exact point, distance, t (source-to-target),
and clamped. RBush search uses bounding-box lower bounds and exact distances;
ties follow insertion order. {scan: true} selects the reference. Empty graphs
return null. Geometry edits update indexes; metadata edits leave them unchanged.
On a quantized graph, an exact projection may round OFF its edge. splitEdge then
throws before mutation; use representable on-edge points or an exact policy.

## Connectivity and cleanup

<!-- example: planarize.ts -->

```ts
import { SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';

// Geometric crossings alone do not create adjacency. Planarize splits ALL cuts.
const graph = new SpatialGraph();
graph.addEdges([
  {
    endpoints: [
      [0, 0],
      [10, 10],
    ],
    attributes: {},
  },
  {
    endpoints: [
      [0, 10],
      [10, 0],
    ],
    attributes: {},
  },
  {
    endpoints: [
      [0, 2],
      [10, 2],
    ],
    attributes: {},
  },
]);
const disconnected = graph.getShortestPath([0, 0], [0, 2]); // null
const report = graph.planarize();
```

Planarize handles crossings/T-junctions/overlap boundaries. Unrepresentable grid
crossings return unresolved points without editing. It is idempotent for
representable intersections. Connected components include isolates. findPaths
covers each edge once, including cycles; findTerminalPaths measures degree in
its induced subset. joinNode preserves shape; cleanup policies such as discarding
small components or repeatedly pruning stubs belong to the application.
mergeNearbyNodes forms transitive clusters with canonical representatives;
maxDisplacement can exceed tolerance. fromPoints uses a caller's connection rule
on every pair of canonical coordinates (O(n²)); it does not merge positions.

## Persistence and adapters

<!-- example: save-and-load.ts -->

```ts
import { SpatialGraph } from '@flatten-js/spatial-graph';

// Spatial JSON is the persistence format: geometry, keys, policies, and metadata.
const graph = new SpatialGraph({ coordinatePrecision: 0 });
graph.addEdge(
  [
    [0, 0],
    [10, 0],
  ],
  { name: 'first' },
);
graph.addEdge(
  [
    [10, 0],
    [10, 10],
  ],
  { name: 'second' },
);
graph.setNodeLabel([0, 0], 'origin');
graph.setGraphAttribute('name', 'network');
const restored = SpatialGraph.fromJSON(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(graph.export())));
```

Spatial JSON schema='spatial-graph', version=2 includes policies, explicit geometry,
keys and graph/node/edge metadata. Values must be JSON-compatible for lossless
JSON.stringify round trips. Callback functions are not serialized; supply factories
and clone hooks when restoring a typed graph. import replaces by default;
{merge: true} uses union rules and requires matching policies.
fromLegacyJSON(data, {coordinatePrecision: 0}) returns {graph, report} with
collision/collapse counts. Legacy weight remains metadata.

Graphology adapters are detached O(V+E) topology copies: top-level x/y and length,
nested data. Nested values follow the shallow-copy/clone-hook convention.
toGraphology currently omits graph-level metadata and spatial policies/factories;
copy graph attributes explicitly and pass policies when importing, if needed.
fromGraphology rejects directed/multi/looped graphs and normalization collisions,
validates x/y, and accepts metadata mapping callbacks. Export anew after edits
for external algorithms. SpatialGraph itself has no inherited Graphology API.
fromGraphology and fromJSON default to NodeAttributes/EdgeAttributes; policy
options do not infer metadata types or require an unrelated factory. Supply
explicit generics for custom metadata schemas, as with the constructor. Required
custom node fields still require createNodeAttributes. See save-and-load.ts.

Flatten adapter names explicitly include Flatten; snapshots expose
toFlattenPoint()/toFlattenSegment(). Segments and straight Multilines are
supported; unsupported arcs/rays/lines throw before batch insertion.
fromGeoJSON accepts Point/LineString/MultiLineString features, maps properties to
metadata, rejects extra dimensions unless dropExtraDimensions is explicit, and
accepts onReport for precision collapses. Geometry is Cartesian, not geodesic.
toGeoJSON emits edge LineStrings plus isolated Points; connected node metadata
is absent from that format. Use spatial JSON when that metadata must survive.

## Further reading

- [Package README](README.md): API groups, installation, migration and release commands.
- [ESM declarations](dist/index.d.ts) / [CJS declarations](dist/index.d.cts): exact public signatures.
- In a source checkout, [examples guide](examples/README.md) maps tasks to ten
  asserting programs; [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) defines contributor conventions.
- Repository-only [refactoring audit](docs/library-refactoring-audit.md) records
  design rationale; [agent-readiness audit](docs/agent-readiness-audit.md) records
  documentation evidence and limitations. These are not installed package files.

1.x NxPoint/NxEdge and inherited Graphology calls were removed. Use Point2D/
Segment2D for geometry and snapshots for elements; use explicit adapters for
Graphology and Flatten. coordinatePrecision: 0 preserves old integer-grid identity.
